answer.evidence: The cabinet is drawn as a flat face-on elevation of a 30-px-wide, 47-row body. The marquee (rows 1-9), screen (10-20), control panel (22-27) and lower body (28-46) are all vertical faces. None has a back rim, an ellipse, an open interior with contents, or a roof plane. The marquee rows 7-9 are dark slot and shadow detail, not a front-edge line over an eave shadow. The grey panel strips beside the wheel are too ambiguous to count as a top surface. The wheel is a face-on circle, not a top-seen opening. It is not a container with an opening, so the kind does not match.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small arcade cabinet, about 2 tiles wide and 3 tall, and it sits at roughly the same scale as the references. Measured facts: 15 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, which is close. Near-flat coverage is 19%, above the cheese stall's 13% and well above the 0% of the hedge, well and bench. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted, a dark red-brown that follows the body, and not a black sticker line. By eye, the cabinet reads as a fairly flat red body with a dark side panel, a blue screen and a small joystick/button cluster. The screen and control deck have some detail, but the red body is a large smooth fill with few grain dots and no per-area highlights or speckle. It has about 3-4 value steps on the main body ramp, against 5-6 on the stall roof and the well. Most of the tile information comes from the screen and controls, not from material texture. It would look slightly flatter and simpler next to the stall and the well, so I judge it shallow in material shading, and when in doubt I fail it.
